To enhance the efficiency of tumor detection, we reduced the dimensionality of CT scans before inputting them into the network. This was compared to a baseline method without data compression. Furthermore, our method compared favorably to existing techniques in aspects like accuracy, representation, and complexity. To facilitate further research, our datasets as well as evaluation metrics are available online. This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which employs unlabeled samples to selectively draw from existing data, fine-tune the model for better performance.
The proposed method seamlessly integrates both high-efficiency dense retrieval and a more effective pair-wise re-ranking process to produce outstanding results, surpassing non-retrieval methods and alternative baselines in our experiments. 
Our findings demonstrate that ReCross successfully transfers labeling information from existing data, even when utilizing the same text for both positive and negative examples, which significantly enhances the model's performance. 
Without sacrificing performance, we also show that ReCross can be adapted to handle smaller, high-quality subset sampling, leading to a scalable solution. 
Our proposed method is easily applicable to both dense and sparse retrieval settings, along with its scalable nature, making it highly suitable for numerous real-world applications. 
The proposed method's efficacy is demonstrated across multiple large datasets including the original data used for pre-training, without requiring any additional labeled data. 
We believe ReCross' versatile and data-efficient nature will serve as a solid foundation for the cross-task generalization of large language models in unsupervised settings. 
The proposed method's code is publicly available at https://github.com/ghrua

As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals struggle to contribute effectively. Our proposed framework, Spatially-Aware Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (SABRA), mitigates the impact of false positives in VRD tasks. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to angular momentum conservation principles. To validate our findings, we updated the constraints based on spectroscopic surface measurements, verified that the detected oscillation patterns align with the previously determined core and outer layer rotation rates, and confirmed that the star exhibits no significant chemical abnormalities. Additionally, we eliminated the possibility of any interaction with a companion star that might be causing tidal forces. Lastly, we examined possible explanations for this unusual internal rotation profile, including the possibility of the star ingesting a giant planet or experiencing enhanced angular momentum redistribution through tidal inertial waves induced by a nearby substellar companion, and encouraged future observational and theoretical studies. This research is particularly relevant to the investigation of the rotational evolution and mixing patterns within giant stars and may serve as a case study for future theoretical modeling. Evaluating the effectiveness of this treatment requires analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT, which can be achieved by accurately defining the treated region through image processing. Although deep learning techniques offer high precision in defining this region, training them requires a large amount of data which can be hard to obtain for a new and emerging treatment such as LITT. In response, this paper proposes an innovative framework called Progressive Brain Lesion Synthesis, consisting of multiple stages to artificially create more training data with various characteristics, thereby enhancing the precision of the therapy evaluation. Furthermore, the paper includes a design for encoding external information that can aid in training and improving segmentation results by integrating a condition and mask embedding block, resulting in better outcomes when compared to common image processing methods, according to experimental data. 

This research paper's innovative framework consisting of progressive brain lesion synthesis and external information integration techniques is applied to a critical medical problem such as LITT, but the proposed methods can be utilized in various fields to enhance the precision of therapy evaluation or other tasks requiring artificial data and external information.

We have investigated a nonparametric Bayesian approach to estimating the nonlinear Hawkes process parameters, obtaining results on the concentration rates of the posterior distribution.
